title: Other path-naming configs can rot behind a green gate
description:
Found by tick cwa (run epic-9pd, attempt 8), which implemented the check for one case and scoped the rest out deliberately.

cwa's check asserts that ./x/... package wildcards named in .github/workflows resolve. The same rot is possible in any config that names paths: CODEOWNERS, lint include lists, release manifests, and bare ./x inputs in workflow run lines (test -x ./scripts/deploy.sh).

Each wants its own false-positive analysis before it becomes a check — a bare path may legitimately be a build output that does not exist at gate time, and a CODEOWNERS entry may name a path that is allowed to be absent. So each is a separate check, not a widening of cwa's.

Low: nothing is known to be rotted today. This is hardening, filed so the shape is not forgotten.
acceptance_criteria: For each config kind adopted, a check that fails the gate when it names a path that cannot resolve, with its false-positive rule recorded; or a recorded decision that the kind is not worth checking
